entries.reason: the words, sentences and paragraphs come from the release's own CFStringTokenizer, so a script the release segments with a smaller dictionary is cut at other places (the two-character Chinese word of the tests is two words on iOS 6), the release's sentence breaker breaks after abbreviations that the port lists by the ones the system's does not break at, and emoji sequences are cut by the port's own rule; a sign that stands alone (™ between spaces) is a word for the system in some contexts and not for the port, and a full stop followed by a symbol ends a sentence for the port and not for the system
entries.effect: a tokenizer of a unit (word, sentence, paragraph, document) of a string answers the ranges of the tokens, their attributes (numeric, symbolic, emoji) and the token that holds an index
entries.source: the host's NaturalLanguage, compared with the port over 1445 checks by tests/backports/host/naturallanguage (natural text in nine scripts, emoji sequences, random text, every index and range), and an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 held to 99 recorded answers by tests/backports/device/naturallanguage.m

entries.reason: the release's tagger names one language for a sentence, so the port votes sentence by sentence, weighted by letters; the language of a clear text is the system's, the probabilities are shares of the letters and not the model's, a sentence too short to judge is judged as the tagger does, and languages the release's tagger does not know are never answered
entries.effect: a recognizer takes strings, then answers the language most of the text is in, or the shares of the languages it saw
entries.source: the host's NaturalLanguage, held to the port for the dominant language of clear text in eight scripts, the shape of the answers, hints, constraints and reset (tests/backports/host/naturallanguage), and an iPad 2 running 6.1.3, where the release's tagger names the language of each sentence
